# Rules: Messaging, notices and other computers

**Covers:** Phone channels, the notifier, the bell's daemon twins, remote agents and the task door: `comm/`, `agents/task_door.py`, remote-agent routes.

How to use this file: read the contents list, then read only the entries your change touches (each line gives the line number where the full text starts). The rules that apply to every change are in the root `CLAUDE.md`. To add a rule, see "Adding a rule" there.

## Rules

- **A remote agent is EDITABLE, and an edit must never eat its credential**
  (v1.164.0). The row offered only Test and Delete, so one wrong character in a
  base URL meant re-entering the record. `PATCH /agents/remote/{name}` +
  `RemoteAgentRegistry.update` do a PARTIAL update. Do NOT "simplify" this back
  into a re-POST of the create body: `upsert` assigns EVERY column including
  `row.secret_name`, and the bearer token is stored encrypted and NEVER returned
  so no UI can prefill it — a re-post therefore sends an empty token and
  silently drops a working credential the user cannot retype, which is worse
  than the retyping it was meant to save. The token has THREE intents and
  conflating any two loses a secret: send one to replace, send NOTHING to keep,
  set `clear_token` to remove. An empty string is "I didn't type one", never
  "delete it" — mutation-proven, and the flag alone is not enough to assert
  (treating `""` as a new token leaves `has_credential` true while overwriting
  the vault entry with an empty string, so tests check the VALUE). `name` is
  deliberately immutable: panels and threads refer to a remote by name
  (`participantKey("remote", name)`), so renaming would orphan them silently.

- **A refused credential is not an empty batch, and at-most-once must
  leave a trace** (v1.231.0, audit Wave 5, AE8/AE14). `TelegramChannel.poll`
  mapped EVERY non-ok answer to `([], offset)` and the IMAP poll wrapped
  `login` in the same blanket `except`, so a revoked bot token was a
  healthy `_tick("inbound", True)` every 15 s forever — the same disease
  as the v1.229.0 sampler, one layer down. A poll raises
  `comm.base.ChannelAuthError` for 401/403 / a refused LOGIN only (a 5xx
  keeps the fail-safe empty batch), `poll_once` turns it into an error
  row + `poll_errors[name]`, and the loop ticks off `poll_verdict` — read
  the status off the RAW response (`_get_raw` + `auth_refusal`), because
  `interpret_json` flattens a 401 to `None` before anyone can see it. The
  inbound offset is still persisted BEFORE handling (a duplicate remote
  action is worse than a dropped reply), but the update in flight rides
  the same write (`inflight_update_id`/`inflight_chat_id`) and is cleared
  only when `_handle` RETURNS — a `CancelledError` at shutdown must leave
  it — so the next boot apologises to that chat and publishes
  `comm.dropped`. Do not "tidy" the clear into a `finally`.

- **A remote agent is a CONVERSATION, both ways** (v1.285.0). The user: "what
  is stopping me from interacting with my remote agents the way I can with
  Slack?" — `RemoteAgentRegistry.run` was one POST carrying only the task text.
  Now `run(..., history=, conversation_id=, reply_to=)`: the OpenAI dialects
  get real prior turns (`messages` / list-form `input`), `http-task` gets
  `conversation_id` + `history` + `reply_to` BESIDE `task` and a bare `{"task"}`
  when none is given (older endpoints see the v1.157.0 body byte for byte); a
  `202` or `{"accepted": true}` with no result answers `{ok, accepted}` and the
  round records "working — will report back" (`pending: True` on the entry).
  `AgentThreads.remote_history` renders the exchange for the remote (user as
  user, its own lines unprefixed, everyone else named); `_speak_remote` returns
  `(reply, extra)`. INWARD: `RemoteAgentRecord.inbound_enabled /
  inbound_secret_name / inbound_url` (additive), `enable_inbound` mints a
  `token_urlsafe(32)` into the vault and returns it ONCE (re-enable ROTATES),
  `verify_inbound` is constant-time via `auth.token_matches` and FAIL-CLOSED;
  `POST /agents/remote/{name}/inbound` is token-EXEMPT in `auth._is_exempt`
  (exactly the `/inbound` leaf — `/inbound/enable|disable` stay guarded) and
  verified in the handler (inbound off → 403, wrong token → 401, not a
  participant of that room → 403, 60/min → 429, 12k chars → 413); files land
  under `<home>/remote-inbox/<agent>/` through `agents/remote_files` (the same
  trust boundary as the delegate tool); the line is a room entry (`inbound:
  True`, `kind`, `documents`) → `AGENT_THREAD_UPDATED` + `REMOTE_MESSAGE`, and
  a room bound to a DAEMON-owned (phone) thread mirrors it there
  (`CommThreadStore.append(extra=)` whitelists `panelWho/panelKind/documents`)
  and sends it to the phone through `d.inbound_poller`. THE PHONE:
  `InboundPoller._remote_addressee` (after the user append in `_handle_chat`)
  routes "@<remote>" — or a follow-up while `setup_json.addressee` is
  `remote:<name>` — to `_handle_remote_chat`: `AgentThreads.for_chat(thread.id)`
  + `run_round(directed=[name], chat_history=store.history_rows(...))` with a
  `SimpleNamespace(platform=)` shim as `d`, the reply appended attributed and
  sent as "<name>: …"; "@jarvis" clears it (`BACK_TO_JARVIS_REPLY`). A LOCAL
  agent named from the phone stays on the Jarvis lane. DASHBOARD: the chat
  page mirrors inbound room entries (`mirrorRoomInbound`, dedupe by `panelAt`,
  on `agent_thread.updated`/`remote.message` for `roomOf(messages)` and on
  open); `panelKind: progress` is a quiet line; `SetupCard`'s remote row has
  Let it message back / Rotate token / Turn off (token shown once, `#inbound-
  minted`). `app.state.d = d` exists so a test can put a poller double where
  the route looks. Pins: `tests/test_remote_conversation_v1285.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/remote-inbound-v1285.test.tsx`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/chat-remote-live-v1285.test.tsx`.
  REVIEW ROUND, each a real defect in the first cut: (1) the packaged daemon
  binds `--host 127.0.0.1` (desktop/main.js) and `auth._host_ok` admits
  loopback Hosts only unless `IRONJARVIS_HOST_ALLOWLIST` is set — so the
  inbound door is unreachable from another machine BY DEFAULT; `enable`
  derives the URL from this machine's LAN address (`_lan_address`, a UDP
  route probe) and answers `reachable: {host_allowed, note}` from the SAME
  `_host_ok`, and the token box + Handbook say the two knobs — never open a
  bind on the user's behalf. (2) `CommThreadStore.history_body` used to hand
  a remote's `panelWho` line to the Jarvis turn as Jarvis's OWN prior turn;
  it now prefixes `agent_line_label(name)` — the exact sentence
  `toRequestMessages` uses, so both lanes tell the model the same thing.
  (3) `rec.enabled` gates inbound too. (4) `remote_agent.inbound.<name>` —
  the vault key uses a "." the remote-name rule cannot produce, because
  `remote_agent_inbound_hermes` collided with the OUTBOUND key of a remote
  named `inbound_hermes`. (5) Unknown room and foreign room both answer 403
  (no id oracle); the response carries file NAMES, not the user's paths;
  `safe_path(inbox, …)` is the second lock; `_fetch` streams and aborts past
  the cap; file posts 10/min + a 512 MB/day inbox budget per agent; phone
  pushes 20 per 10 min (the thread keeps every line). (6) `mirrorRoomInbound`
  captures `chatGenRef` and re-checks `roomOf(current)` after the fetch and
  is single-flight per room. (7) "@jarvis <question>" clears the sticky AND
  falls through to the Jarvis turn (`_words_beyond_mentions`); a remote named
  in the same text wins. (8) `remote_history` skips `pending` notes (Jarvis's
  words about the remote, not the remote's).

  handoff=True)`; never `consult`) and the `delegate_remote` tool open a
  report-back ROOM when the remote may message back

  `{"accepted": true}` is its own outcome: `ToolResult(ok, output=

  possibly cut untrusted fence (the event's `_short`) for the card and the log

- **A destination's Edit KEEPS what is saved; two-way says why it cannot hear
  the user** (v1.427.6, a USER BUG: "i need to re-enter the tokens because they
  are cleared when i go to edit" and "i couldnt message it back"). Edit
  re-submits `POST /comm/channels`, which rebuilt the config from the form
  alone; the form never holds a secret or the allowlist's ids, so every edit
  DROPPED the Slack tokens and the allowlist, and an empty allowlist means
  `SlackSocketMode.candidates()` never arms the pump (the live log said
  "slack socket mode disarmed"). Now, for an existing destination of the SAME
  type, a blank field keeps its stored value (secrets by their `<key>_secret`
  reference), a key in `config.clear` is removed (its vault row deleted after
  the save), a typed value replaces; NEW secrets are written only after the
  whole save is valid (a refused edit never swaps a working token). `GET
  /comm/channels` rows add `saved_fields` (names only), `values` (plain values
  except `HIDDEN_VALUES` = webhook_url, allowed_senders) and `two_way_note`
  (`routes/comm.two_way_note`: two-way on with no allowlist / no way to hear
  Slack / no bot token; also on the POST answer). Slack gains `chat_enabled`;
  the manifest turns on `features.app_home` messages tab (not read-only). The
  page seeds `values`, says "Saved — leave blank to keep it", sends `clear`
  for "Remove the saved one" and for an erased shown value, opens Advanced
  when saved fields live there. Pins: `tests/test_slack_keep_tokens_v14276.py`
  (8 mutations red), `dashboard/__tests__/notifications-edit-keeps-v1427-6.test.tsx`
  (7 mutations red).
- **A pairing is a remote agent plus two vault tokens, kept all or nothing,
  and only the pairing card changes it** (v1.497.0, vision plan leap 7
  Phase 1). `peers/` (codes, store, link) + `daemon/routes/peers.py`;
  the card is `dashboard/components/settings/OtherComputers.tsx` (Settings ›
  Connections › Your other computers). Each side keeps a `PeerRecord`, its
  own token for the other (`peer.<id>.in`, checked at the task door and the
  unpair door) and the other's (`peer.<id>.out`), and a `RemoteAgentRecord`
  of the same name (kind http-task, base_url the other's
  `/agents/task-door/task`, message-back on), so "@name", delegation and
  answers coming home reuse the remote-agent code untouched. Hold these:
  - `/peers/pair` and `/peers/unpair` are the ONLY exempt doors, matched
    exactly in `daemon/auth._is_exempt`, and for POST only (`_exempt_for`;
    v1.499.1: a DELETE there reached `DELETE /peers/{name}` with no token for
    a pairing named "pair"). Pair is checked by the code, unpair
    by that peer's in-token. Both read the body no further than
    `PAIR_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (stream, never `request.body()`), share the
    ten-tries-a-minute budget, and answer a failure in WORDS, never the app's
    500 envelope (it carries the exception's text to an unauthenticated
    caller).
  - The address kept for the other computer is the TCP client's IP plus the
    port it sent, never anything else in the body, and it is read BEFORE the
    code (a request that cannot be placed never uses the code up).
  - The door that took the code answers within `routes/peers.KEEP_MAX_S`
    (10 s, under the joiner's `link.PAIR_TIMEOUT_S` 15 s); a keep that lands
    after that is taken back (`_take_back_late`), so a slow vault or SQLite
    never leaves a pairing on one computer only (v1.499.1).
  - `PeerStore.add` is all or nothing (`_undo_half`), and a remote agent
    made under the name meanwhile is never overwritten (`NameTaken`). When the
    joining side cannot keep a pairing the other already kept, it calls
    `link.unpair` with the token it was given (`join_failed_words`).
  - `free_name` avoids every name "@" already reaches (built-in and custom
    agents, `JARVIS_MENTIONS`, remotes, pairings), case-insensitively,
    because `resolve_target` prefers a local agent. The same computer at the
    same address replaces its pairing even under a `-2` name.
  - A paired remote is refused at `POST /agents/remote` (any case), PATCH of
    base_url/kind/token, DELETE, inbound enable/disable/rotate
    (`PAIRED_REMOTE_REFUSAL`); PATCH inbound_url stays allowed on purpose.
  - The task door's `_door_check` returns `(door, peer)`: a peer token gets in
    even with the manual door off, and the caller is the peer's name.
  - Codes live in memory only (`PairingCodes`, created under `_CODES_LOCK`):
    10 minutes, one use, five wrong tries end it and publish
    `peer.code_ended` so the showing screen takes it down.
  Pins: `tests/test_peers_v1497.py`, `tests/test_peers_review_v1497.py`
  (19 of 19 mutations red), `dashboard/__tests__/other-computers-v1497.test.tsx`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/other-computers-review-v1497.test.tsx` (9 of 9 red).
  OPEN: on one network the traffic is plain http, like the manual door
  (Tailscale encrypts; the Handbook says so); anyone on the network can burn
  a shown code or the shared try budget; httpx honours `HTTP_PROXY`; a
  re-pair that fails after the old pairing was replaced loses the old one;
  not yet driven between two real PCs on the packaged build. Phase 2 (what a
  paired computer may do) is not built.

- **An email sender is trusted only with proof from the receiving provider** (v1.499.3 review). `channels.sender_proof` reads the TOPMOST `Authentication-Results`: an aligned `dkim=pass`, `dmarc=pass` or aligned `spf=pass`. Without it the sender is `unverified:<addr>`, never authorised (no commands, approvals, rules or sessions), logged once without the body. OPEN: Microsoft 365 mail inside one tenant can carry `dkim=none`, so the owner's own internal mail may be refused; `X-MS-Exchange-Organization-AuthAs: Internal` is not trusted yet. Pins: `tests/test_review_fixes_daemon_v1499_3.py`, `tests/test_cx05_email.py`.

- **A task from another computer is never the owner's: it runs with none of this computer's memory, keeps only a short list of tools, reads only its own folder, and its answer goes only to the pairing it came from, by id** (v1.509.0, second review F1, F5, F6, F14).
  `runtime.run_is_remote` (the `remote:` origin, or the `REMOTE_RUN` context
  value so delegated helpers inherit it) gates `skip_memory`, the profile,
  the notebook and the client wall's named set. Tools: an ALLOW list,
  `core/trust.REMOTE_RUN_KEEP` (`remote_run_keeps`); everything else is
  refused by name through the ledgered low-trust path, an app pack's tools
  and a tool added tomorrow included. A deny list was tried first and missed
  the allow-tier readers (`browser_read_page`, `pane_read`,
  `mcp_read_resource`, `config_list`, `list_folder`). Reads:
  `core/fs_policy.confine_reads` confines `fs_read_ok` / `fs_path_allowed`
  to the run's folder for the run and everything awaited inside it. A tool
  joins the keep list only if it is pure, works inside `ctx.workspace`
  through `safe_path`, or reads through `fs_read_ok`; a reader that takes a
  path is added to the parametrized test, which drives it at a real file
  outside the folder. The reply spec carries `door`, `peer_id`, `address`
  and `from`: a removed pairing sends nothing, Remove stops its runs
  (`Orchestrator.stop_with_reason`, the `remote_peer` option), a task from
  another address is recorded as `heard_from` and never answered at the old
  one, and the address is NEVER updated from a request (a captured token
  would redirect answers). Both doors take one try per source address
  before any database or vault read; the task window is per caller.
  `_reply_files` sends only files inside the run's or a worker's folder. A
  peer's (and any @-agent's) line in a chat reaches the model fenced
  (`chat_refs.fence_agent_lines`, called in `chat_turn._plan_context` for
  both lanes). Left open: a pairing kept under a host NAME cannot be
  compared with a source address; `/chat/compact` builds its own history
  and still sees an agent's line unfenced.
  Pins: `tests/test_second_review_remote_run_v1509.py`,
  `tests/test_second_review_pairing_v1509.py`.
